c.tagline: Turkish Riviera beach resort crowned by a Seljuk castle on a rocky peninsula

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis run on meters within the city; agree a fixed price in advance for trips to Gazipaşa Airport or nearby towns.

emergency.note: 112 is Turkey's general emergency line covering ambulance and fire; dial 155 to reach police directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Resort nightlife scams and touts; drink-spiking

hood_desc: Kale (Castle Hill) is Alanya's historic core, a fortified Seljuk-era peninsula with panoramic sea views, the Red Tower, and narrow lanes of Ottoman houses. It's the most atmospheric base for sightseeing, though steep and quieter at night.
Cleopatra Beach and the adjoining town center form Alanya's main tourist hub, with its famous sweep of soft sand, harbor-front promenade, and a dense cluster of restaurants, bars, and shops.
Damlataş sits just west of the harbor around its namesake stalactite cave, a low-key residential-meets-tourist pocket handy for both the beach and the old town.
Mahmutlar, a few kilometers east, is a fast-growing expat and long-stay retiree enclave with a long beach promenade, budget apartments, and a large Northern European and Russian-speaking community.
Kestel is a quieter, mostly residential seafront district east of the center, popular with families seeking a calmer stretch of beach away from the nightlife.

water.note: Stick to bottled water, as nearly all locals and hotels do.

transit.hours: Minibuses run roughly 7am-midnight along the coastal routes
transit.pay: Cash paid to driver, small fixed fares by zone
transit.map: No official app; routes are shown on destination signs in the windshield
transit.note: Alanya has no metro or tram; shared dolmuş minibuses and city buses (ALTAŞ) are the main public transport, supplemented by taxis and rental scooters.

bus: Frequent intercity coaches connect Alanya's otogar to Antalya, Istanbul, and other Turkish cities

tip.r: Round up or add ~10% at restaurants; not required for taxis but appreciated

landmarks: Alanya Castle (Alanya Kalesi)
A Seljuk fortress crowning a rocky peninsula, its six kilometres of crenellated walls enclosing Byzantine chapels and dizzying Mediterranean panoramas.
Kizil Kule (Red Tower)
Alanya's octagonal red-brick symbol, a 33-metre Seljuk defensive tower from 1226 guarding the harbour and housing a small ethnographic museum.
Cleopatra Beach
Two kilometres of famously fine golden sand and crystalline water where, legend claims, Mark Antony gifted the shore to Cleopatra herself.
Damlatas Cave
A chamber of dripping orange stalactites discovered in 1948 beside Cleopatra Beach, its humid microclimate long prized for easing asthma.
Tersane (Seljuk Shipyard)
The Mediterranean's only surviving Seljuk dockyard, five stone-arched galleries from 1228 opening dramatically onto the turquoise sea beneath the castle.
Alanya Teleferik (Cable Car)
A scenic gondola gliding from Cleopatra Beach up to the castle ramparts, unfurling postcard views over the bay and red-roofed old town.
Dim Cave (Dim Magarasi)
One of Turkey's most beautiful show caves, a 360-metre gallery of glittering stalagmites ending at a mirror-still underground lake.
Dim River (Dimcay)
A chilly mountain river east of town where riverside platform restaurants serve fresh trout above jade pools shaded by pine-clad gorges.
Sapadere Canyon
A 400-metre-deep gorge in the Taurus foothills threaded by wooden walkways past waterfalls and icy natural swimming pools.
Alanya Harbour and Lovers' Cave Boat Tours
Wooden gulets depart the palm-lined marina to circle the castle peninsula, visiting Pirates' Cave, Lovers' Cave, and phosphorescent grottoes.

train.note: There is no railway on this stretch of the Mediterranean coast - the nearest TCDD stations are far inland at Konya or Isparta. Travel to and from Alanya is by coach, car or a flight into Gazipaşa-Alanya or Antalya airports.

bus.note: No international coaches leave Alanya; long-distance runs to Europe start in Istanbul. The otogar west of the centre has frequent services to Antalya (about 2 hours), Konya, Ankara and Istanbul on Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/), Metro Turizm (https://www.metroturizm.com.tr/en) and Alanya Seyahat; book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/). Dolmuş minibuses run along the coast road to Side and Manavgat.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from Alanya. The harbour runs day boats and pirate-ship cruises along the coast and to the sea caves below the castle, which are excursions rather than transport, and the nearest crossing to Northern Cyprus sails from Taşucu, well to the east.

half.name: Side
half.blurb: Ancient port town whose Roman temple of Apollo columns stand right on the Mediterranean shoreline at sunset.

half.name: Antalya
half.blurb: Turkish Riviera hub with a restored old quarter, harbor, and waterfalls, roughly ninety minutes up the coast.

half.name: Manavgat Waterfall
half.blurb: Wide, low cascade on the Manavgat River popular for riverside lunches and short boat trips.

full.name: Pamukkale
full.blurb: Cascading white travertine terraces of mineral pools beside the ruins of ancient Hierapolis, several hours inland.
